messages:
Jamie: FYI — noticed a bunch of fallback churn during the midnight spike when prefetching was on. Some tenants hit the fallback path repeatedly and we saw wasted tokens + jitter in tail latency. Opening a thread to align on quick mitigation vs longer refactor.
Maya: Ack. I pulled the traces — looks like most fallbacks happen when prefetch window overlaps with a big burst (10-100x). The issue: prefetch enqueues extra requests, then admission decides to evict them when capacity tightens.
Maya: snippet from the logs:
```
batcher: prefetch enqueued 46 reqs (threshold=0.7)
admission: drop 38 prefetch reqs (reason=slot-pressure, headroom=12)
metrics: fallback_count++
```
Maya: So wasted token spend + extra scheduling churn. :grimacing:
Oleg: Two quick knobs we can toggle: 1) prefetch size cap per-tenant, 2) conservative fallback cooldown so we don't immediately re-prefetch. Both cheap to ship.
Oleg: tradeoffs: smaller prefetch -> less hit rate on cache warmup, more cold-start latency; longer cooldown -> slower recovery after transient load.
Jamie: Agreed. What's smallest change to reduce churn quickly?
Maya: I can do a canary: clamp prefetch to max( N, floor(tenant_quota * 0.2) ) and add a 10s backoff per-tenant after fallback. Should cut the oscillation.
Rik: Short term fine. Medium-term we should separate "prefetching" from the main admission queue. Give prefetches a soft lane with own credits and preemption semantics. That prevents head-of-line evictions affecting live requests.
Rik: Sketch: separate queue with tokens funded by an elastic budget (small % of GPU throughput). Prefetches only run when budget > threshold; budget refilled slowly. If overloaded, prefetch queue stops without touching primary queue.
Sasha: Sounds safe. Questions: how do we detect when prefetch warmed the KV vs when it created useless load? We need telemetry to measure prefetch effectiveness: hit rate, latency saved, tokens wasted.
Maya: Agreed — add metrics: prefetch_enqueued, prefetch_consumed, prefetch_evicted, prefetch_cache_hit, prefetch_tokens_wasted. Add a derived signal: effective_prefetch_rate = prefetch_cache_hit / prefetch_consumed.
Oleg: Also consider sampling-based prefetching: only prefetch for X% of requests for low-importance tenants, or exponentially backoff on repeated evictions.
Jamie: Good. For the quick canary, prioritize: 1) clamp size, 2) 10s cooldown, 3) surface new metrics to the console. Who can ship canary tonight?
Maya: I can cut the patch and push a canary config to dedicated region A by EOD. Will push metrics to /metrics/prefetch_* and a small dashboard.
ci-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started for batcher-service v3.14.2-canary to region-a (3 hosts).
Oleg: If we see lowered fallback_count and reduced wasted tokens in the first 30m, we can roll to prod. If tail latency spikes, revert. Keep an eye on token-billing alerts.
Rik: Long-term RFC notes (quick bullets):
- separate prefetch lane with soft credits
- admission API: expose PreemptIfPressure flag so callers can opt-in to preemptable prefetches
- telemetry: per-tenant prefetch ROI and stale-prefetch ratio
- config: per-tenant prefetch budget + global cap
Sasha: For the RFC we should document interface boundaries: prefetching is an implementation of warmup, not a client-visible request type. Keep the public admission API unchanged; add internal lane semantics only. That avoids churn in SDKs.
Jamie: Nice. Let's do the canary first then follow-up with an RFC doc (short). Maya, post the canary dashboard link when ready.
Maya: Will do. Pushing grafana panel and a small alert rule: if prefetch_tokens_wasted_rate > 0.2 AND fallback_count_rate > 5/min => pager to eng-runtime (severity=low).
Jamie: :thumbsup: thanks all.
Maya: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/prefetch-surge (canary panel)
ci-bot: deploybot: canary rollout complete (3/3 hosts). Monitoring for 30m.
